name: Pharmaceutical safety and efficacy
payer: Sponsor funds trials and, since 1992, pays user fees for review.
access: Regulator receives full trial data; inspects sites and labs.
publication: Approval decisions and labels public; trial registration and results reporting mandated since 2007.
ai_analogue: The Industrial Bio-Test fraud is the direct precedent for regulating the testing labs themselves; Good Laboratory Practice was the response. Trial registration is the precedent for evaluation registries.

milestones.event: Pure Food and Drug Act: labeling and adulteration rules.
Elixir sulfanilamide kills more than 100 people.
Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act: pre-market safety review.

milestones.trigger_criterion: Thousands of birth defects and deaths

milestones.event: Sponsors design and run the efficacy trials the regulator reviews; contract research organizations grow from the 1970s.
Kefauver-Harris Amendment: proof of efficacy, controlled trials, informed consent.
Adequate and well-controlled trials required as the evidentiary standard.
Industrial Bio-Test Laboratories found to have falsified safety studies for hundreds of products.
Good Laboratory Practice regulations govern the conduct and inspection of nonclinical testing labs.
PDUFA: sponsors pay user fees that fund FDA review (payment moves toward the assessed party).
FDA rule on financial disclosure by clinical investigators (21 CFR Part 54).
FDAAA mandates trial registration and results reporting on ClinicalTrials.gov.

status: seed; secondary sources; verify each milestone against a primary source before citing in the paper

mechanisms.note: Sponsor funds trials and user fees; FDA reviews and inspects labs under GLP; trials registered publicly.
